text.p: Italian bonds and BTP futures started easier and continued to drift lower following the slump in U.S. T-bonds on Friday and concern over the continued strength in the dollar, dealers said.

They added that European bond markets were still reacted to the sharp falls across the Atlantic on Friday after strong jobs figures and a NAPM economy survey which pushed up expectations of a possible U.S. interest rate rise.
"This is just a continuation of Friday's fall, but BPTs are underperformering and the spread over bunds is back out above 100 basis points," said one dealer on the LIFFE market.
The dollar held above 1.86 against the German mark putting many European bond markets on the defensive, dealers added.
On the Italian cash market, the 10-year BTP/bund spread on the new benchmark July 2007 BTP widened out to 103 basis points by 0745 GMT.

German finance minister Theo Waigel was quoted in a German weekly magazine as saying that a delay to Europe's single currency would kill off the project altogether. "Whoever calls for a five-year delay must know that the project would be then be dead," he said.
